rules.rule: Begin with basic nodes and gradually add more complex nodes as you become comfortable. Experiment with presets before refining.
Erosion is the primary process through which we turn abstract and geometric shapes into believable terrains.
Chain erosion strategically: apply multiple erosion passes sequentially with decreasing duration rather than relying on single-pass processing.
Use selective processing with masks for specific flow control when needing precise major flow lines.
Erosion is not mandatory as the final step. Modern workflows use LookDev nodes (Canyonizer, Stacks, Anastomosis, Shear) for alternative effects.
Apply Thermal/Thermal2 simulation before water-based erosion for realistic landslide patterns on slopes.
Use Tabs to separate concerns — split complex graphs across multiple tabs by function: main shape, colors, masks, and exports.
Organize related nodes into collapsible Groups with colors and icons to clarify workflow logic.
Use Portals to connect nodes across vast gaps without visible connections, reducing clutter.
Use Auto Layout (F4) to untangle dense graph areas while preserving logic.
Bookmark critical nodes (key generators, export points) for instant navigation in large graphs.
Suspend the engine (backtick key) when making multiple edits to avoid long reprocessing.
Lock Preview (F key) to pin a specific node and prevent full recalculation when testing upstream changes.
Bake heavy/finalized nodes at high resolution to reduce computational load during editing. Resolution options: 1024, 2048 (default), 4096, 8192.
Use Build Swarm (close Gaea UI first) for full-resolution builds — the UI takes up large portions of RAM, CPU, and GPU.
Enable "Purge Unnecessary Cache During Build" in Options > Build to reduce RAM usage on memory-constrained systems.
Use Build Path Tokens (<FileLocation>, [Filename], [Timestamp], [+++]) for organized, reproducible output paths.
Add Regions to isolate and upscale high-detail areas without rebuilding the entire terrain.
Choose build subdivision based on quality vs speed: None for fast builds, Balanced for standard, Slower for production.
Apply ColorErosion after terrain shape is finalized to tint worn surfaces realistically without altering geometry.
Use Normals, Curvature, and Slope nodes as masks to selectively apply effects to specific terrain features.
Start coloring pipeline with TextureBase → SatMap, then layer additional color nodes with Combine.
Use chained creation shortcodes (m,e2,e2,tb,sm) to rapidly build linear sequences: Mountain→Erosion2→Erosion2→TextureBase→SatMap.
Drag output-to-output to auto-insert a Combine node — avoids manual setup.
Push nodes with Ctrl+Shift drag to shift them rightward for quick graph reorganization.
Set correct Underlays on secondary branches (right-click > Use as Underlay or press G) to prevent incorrect terrain display.
Avoid modifying nodes upstream of an Underlay — all intermediate nodes rebuild, causing slowdowns at 2K+ resolution.
Erosion2 algorithm is resolution-independent — 512x512 previews match 4K/8K output quality.
Enable Deterministic option on erosion for reproducible results (slower but identical outputs).
Combine Warp with primitive shapes (RadialGradient, heightmaps) for realistic detail generation.
